description: An introduction to force, its SI unit, types of forces, their effects, balanced and unbalanced forces, and the difference between mass and weight.

mcq.questionText: What is the SI unit of force?
mcq.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton.

mcq.questionText: A force is best defined as a:

options.text: Push or pull acting on a body
Quantity of matter in a body

mcq.explanation: A force is a push or a pull that one body exerts on another.

mcq.questionText: Which type of force pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth?
mcq.explanation: Gravitational force is the pull of the Earth on objects, giving them weight.

mcq.questionText: The force that opposes the motion of two surfaces sliding over each other is called:
mcq.explanation: Friction is a force that opposes relative motion between surfaces in contact.

mcq.questionText: The upward force exerted by a liquid on an object placed in it is called:
mcq.explanation: Upthrust (buoyant force) acts upward on an object immersed in a fluid.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an effect of a force?

options.text: Changing the shape of a body
Changing the speed of a moving body
Changing the colour of a body

mcq.explanation: A force can change shape, speed or direction, but it does not change colour.

mcq.questionText: When two or more forces acting on a body cancel out and produce no change in motion, the forces are said to be:
mcq.explanation: Balanced forces have a zero resultant, so the body stays at rest or moves at constant velocity.

mcq.questionText: The pulling force transmitted through a stretched string or rope is called:
mcq.explanation: Tension is the force carried along a string, rope or cable when it is pulled tight.

mcq.questionText: Which instrument is commonly used to measure force in the laboratory?
mcq.explanation: A spring balance measures force (such as weight) using the extension of a spring.

mcq.questionText: The weight of a body of mass 5 kg, taking g = 10 N/kg, is:
mcq.explanation: Using W = mg = 5 kg x 10 N/kg = 50 N.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about mass is correct?

options.text: Mass changes from place to place
Mass is the quantity of matter in a body and stays constant

mcq.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, measured in kilograms, and does not change with location.

mcq.questionText: A magnet attracting an iron nail is an example of which type of force?
mcq.explanation: Magnetic force is the attraction or repulsion exerted by a magnet on magnetic materials.

mcq.questionText: A book resting on a table experiences an upward force from the table surface. This force is called the:
mcq.explanation: The normal reaction is the force a surface exerts perpendicular to itself on an object resting on it.

mcq.questionText: When the forces acting on a body are unbalanced, the body will:

options.text: Move with a change in its motion (accelerate)

mcq.explanation: Unbalanced forces have a non-zero resultant, which changes the body's speed or direction.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a way of reducing friction between moving parts of a machine?
mcq.explanation: Lubricants such as oil and grease form a thin layer that reduces friction between surfaces.

fib.questionText: A force is a push or a _____ acting on a body.
fib.explanation: A force is defined as a push or a pull exerted on a body.

fib.questionText: The SI unit of force is the _____.
The force of attraction of the Earth on a body is called _____ force.
fib.explanation: Gravitational force pulls bodies towards the centre of the Earth.

fib.questionText: The force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact is called _____.
fib.explanation: Friction acts opposite to the direction of relative motion of surfaces.

fib.questionText: The upward force that a liquid exerts on an object placed in it is called _____.
fib.explanation: Upthrust is the buoyant force acting upward on an immersed object.

fib.questionText: The weight of a body is calculated using the formula W = m _____.
fib.explanation: Weight equals mass times gravitational field strength, W = mg.

fib.questionText: The quantity of matter contained in a body is called its _____.
fib.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in a body, measured in kilograms.

fib.questionText: A body of mass 2 kg has a weight of _____ N when g = 10 N/kg.
fib.explanation: W = mg = 2 kg x 10 N/kg = 20 N.

fib.questionText: When the resultant of all forces on a body is zero, the forces are said to be _____.
fib.explanation: Balanced forces produce no change in the motion of a body.

fib.questionText: The pulling force in a stretched rope or string is called _____.
fib.explanation: Tension is the force transmitted along a taut rope or string.

tf.questionText: Force is a push or a pull acting on a body.
tf.explanation: This is the basic definition of a force.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of force is the kilogram.
tf.explanation: The SI unit of force is the newton; the kilogram is the unit of mass.

tf.questionText: Friction always acts in the same direction as the motion of a body.
tf.explanation: Friction acts opposite to the direction of motion, opposing it.

tf.questionText: Weight is the force of gravity acting on a body.
tf.explanation: Weight is the gravitational pull on a body, given by W = mg.

tf.questionText: The mass of a body changes when it is taken from the Earth to the Moon.
tf.explanation: Mass is constant everywhere; only weight changes because gravity differs.

tf.questionText: Balanced forces acting on a stationary body keep it at rest.
tf.explanation: When forces are balanced the resultant is zero, so a body at rest stays at rest.

tf.questionText: A force can change the shape of a body.
tf.explanation: Forces can deform bodies, for example stretching a spring or squashing clay.

tf.questionText: Lubrication increases friction between moving surfaces.
tf.explanation: Lubrication reduces friction by separating the surfaces with a film of oil.

tf.questionText: Upthrust acts in a downward direction on an object floating in water.
tf.explanation: Upthrust acts upward, opposing the weight of the object.

tf.questionText: Unbalanced forces can change the speed or direction of a moving body.
tf.explanation: An unbalanced force has a non-zero resultant, which causes acceleration.

summary.correctAnswer: A force is a push or a pull acting on a body.
summary.explanation: Force can start, stop or change the motion or shape of a body.
Force is measured in newtons using a spring balance.

summary.correctAnswer: A force can change the shape, speed or direction of a body.
summary.explanation: It can also start a body moving or bring a moving body to rest.

summary.correctAnswer: The pull of the Earth on a body, giving it weight.
summary.explanation: It always acts towards the centre of the Earth.

summary.correctAnswer: A force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact.
summary.explanation: It can be reduced by lubrication, smoothing or using ball bearings.

summary.correctAnswer: The upward force a fluid exerts on an object placed in it.
summary.explanation: Upthrust makes objects feel lighter in water and can cause floating.

summary.correctAnswer: Mass is the matter in a body (kg); weight is the force of gravity on it (N).
summary.explanation: Mass is constant, but weight varies with gravitational field strength.

summary.correctAnswer: W = mg, where g is about 10 N/kg on Earth.
summary.explanation: Weight in newtons equals mass in kilograms times g.

summary.correctAnswer: Balanced forces give zero resultant; unbalanced forces give a non-zero resultant.
summary.explanation: Balanced forces cause no change in motion; unbalanced forces cause acceleration.

summary.correctAnswer: Gravitational, magnetic, frictional, tension, normal reaction and upthrust.
summary.explanation: These are common forces studied at Form 1 level.

hoq.questionText: An astronaut has a mass of 70 kg. Taking g = 10 N/kg on Earth and g = 1.6 N/kg on the Moon, what is the difference between the astronaut's weight on Earth and on the Moon?
hoq.explanation: Earth weight = 70 x 10 = 700 N; Moon weight = 70 x 1.6 = 112 N; difference = 700 - 112 = 588 N.

hoq.questionText: A box is pushed along the floor with a force of 50 N to the right, while friction of 20 N acts on it. What is the resultant force and its direction?
hoq.explanation: The forces are unbalanced; resultant = 50 N - 20 N = 30 N acting to the right, in the direction of the push.

hoq.questionText: A stone weighs 30 N in air but appears to weigh 18 N when fully immersed in water. What is the upthrust acting on the stone?
hoq.explanation: Upthrust = weight in air - apparent weight in water = 30 N - 18 N = 12 N.
